comparison: Perfect overlap on methodological claims C113-C116. OpenEval finds methods well-supported and properly justified. Peer reviewers accept technical quality but raise concerns about potential SBEM artifacts and error rates, expressing uncertainty about method limitations that OpenEval does not address.

Near-perfect overlap on auxiliary cell morphology claims C80-C90. Both evaluations support these structural observations. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of comparisons to previous work, while peer reviewers accept findings without challenge as complementary anatomical details.

OpenEval R2 covers C6-C11 (sensillum-level measurements), while peer R1 covers C6-C18 (including neuron-level measurements from OpenEval R3). Both strongly support the quantitative measurements and population-level survey demonstrating heterogeneity. Peer review emphasizes the comprehensive nature and acceptance by all reviewers.

OpenEval R3 addresses C12-C18 (morphometric measurements and correlations), which are included in peer R1's broader assessment of C6-C18. Both support the statistical analyses and measurements. OpenEval specifically validates the lack of correlation and independent regulation inference.

Strong overlap on ab1C morphological characterization (C32-C41). Both evaluations strongly support the novel findings of sheet-like structures and categorization scheme. Peer review emphasizes the convincing case for unique dendritic morphology, while OpenEval validates against previous TEM studies.

OpenEval R8 covers morphometric comparisons C42-C47, while peer R2 includes these in broader assessment of ab1C morphology (C27-C47, C91-C92). Both support the quantitative findings. OpenEval highlights the dramatic SA/V ratio increase as key finding; peer review emphasizes overall morphological uniqueness.

OpenEval R6 addresses C27-C31 (novel morphological observations), partially overlapping with peer R2's broader ab1C assessment. Both support these observations as central findings. OpenEval emphasizes comparison to other sensillum types; peer review focuses on overall uniqueness of ab1C morphology.

Strong overlap on ab1D morphological diversity claims C54-C59. Both evaluations support the findings with adequate sample size. OpenEval notes the notable finding of unbranched basiconic ORNs; peer review emphasizes convincing demonstration of heterogeneity in both populations.

OpenEval marks functional interpretations C77-C78 as speculative; peer review acknowledges descriptive nature and speculation about biophysical properties.
